draft.title: Motivation and arousal
card: comes from inside the person. They play because they enjoy it or find it satisfying.
comes from outside rewards, such as trophies, money, praise or a place in a team.
Arousal is how alert and physically stirred up an athlete feels, from very calm to very excited. Performance is usually best at a moderate level of arousal.
Too little arousal can leave an athlete flat and slow to react. Too much, especially when it brings anxiety (worry and tension), can harm performance.
draft.remember: Motivation is about why you play. Arousal is about how stirred up you feel, and a moderate level usually works best.

a.q: Dani swims on cold mornings only because she loves the feeling of gliding through the water. What type of motivation is this?
a.why: Dani is driven by her own enjoyment, so her motivation is intrinsic. It would be extrinsic only if she swam for a reward such as a medal or money.
a.clue: Where does her reason for swimming come from?

b.q: Before a netball final, Priya feels so tense and worried that her passes go astray, though she trained well. Which explanation fits best?
opts: Her arousal is too high and anxiety is harming her skills
Her arousal is moderate, so her skills should hold up
Her arousal is too low, so she is flat and slow to react
Her extrinsic motivation is too weak to play well
b.why: Tension and worry point to arousal that is too high, with anxiety harming her passing. Low arousal would leave her flat, not tense, and the question says nothing about rewards.
b.clue: Does tense and worried sound like too much or too little arousal?

b.best: Her arousal is too high and anxiety is harming her skills

check.summary: No problems found. The card matches the standard intrinsic/extrinsic and inverted-U ideas, and both questions have one clear right answer.
